headline: Highest risk is B’s broad filesystem/network privileges; A is read-only and isolated, so pairwise injection and leakage are limited but capability conflict and cascading misuse remain possible.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: A cannot read files, use clipboard, or accept MCP, and B has no documented shared channel back into A. B can emit stdout and act on files, but A has no ingestion surface shown, so a prompt-injection bridge is not evidenced. Uncertainty is low because both profiles lack a shared communication path.
conditions: IF a shared filesystem or clipboard bridge is added between A and B, injection risk becomes plausible.
IF A is configured to ingest B's stdout or files as instructions, reassess upward.
mitigations: Keep A and B on separate workspaces.
Do not pipe B stdout into A prompts.
Disable any future clipboard bridge between the agents.
requires-engineering: add provenance tagging if a shared channel is introduced.

B_data_leakage.rationale: A touches no data classes and has no filesystem or network access, while B can read/write files and has broad egress. There is no documented shared workspace, so direct leakage from A to B is not shown. The main concern is B handling sensitive container artifacts and registry credentials, not exfiltration from A.
conditions: IF A and B are placed on the same shared filesystem, leakage risk increases.
IF B is given access to A-generated documents containing secrets, B may exfiltrate them via broad egress.
mitigations: Keep B away from any shared secret-bearing directory.
Mount separate volumes for A and B.
Redact secrets before handing artifacts to B.
Restrict B egress with a firewall rule.
requires-engineering: add per-file access controls.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: A has no write or network capabilities, but B can write files, execute shell, and spawn subprocesses. If both are pointed at the same mutable directory, B can overwrite A’s outputs or artifacts. The conflict is one-sided but real in default CLI workflows; uncertainty favors medium because shared workspace isolation is not documented.
conditions: IF A and B share a writable directory, file clobbering becomes possible.
IF B is run against artifacts produced by A without locking, race conditions can corrupt outputs.
mitigations: Use separate output directories.
Run B after A completes, not concurrently.
Make A outputs read-only before B starts.
Avoid shared git working trees.
requires-engineering: add locking around shared artifacts.

D_cascading_error.rationale: A is a document-processing agent and B is an interactive CLI that can execute commands. If B consumes A’s outputs as authoritative, A’s mistakes can cascade into destructive container actions or incorrect image changes. No verification step is documented, so the pathway exists by default inference, though not directly evidenced.
conditions: IF B uses A-generated text or artifacts as authoritative input, cascading errors can propagate.
IF B executes commands derived from A output without human review, impact increases.
mitigations: Require human review of A outputs before B acts.
Add a validation checklist for B inputs.
Limit B to dry-run mode when consuming A artifacts.
Log and diff A-to-B handoffs.
requires-engineering: add schema validation between agents.

E_compliance.rationale: B explicitly handles registry credentials, certificate private keys, and environment variables, while A’s profile shows no data classes touched and no residency controls. Because B can process sensitive artifacts and has broad egress, compliance risk exists if regulated data is routed through it. A is not cited as a source of compliance burden because its profile shows no such data handling.
conditions: IF regulated secrets or private keys are processed by B, retention and residency controls must be enforced.
IF EU personal data is routed through B without a DPA, compliance risk increases.
mitigations: Exclude regulated data from B inputs.
Set short retention on B logs.
Store secrets in a dedicated vault, not in artifacts.
Document data flow and residency for B.
requires-engineering: implement deletion/export workflows.
